### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Note 2 restatement footnote** `[p. 44]`: Reclassification of R439m into turnover/COGS and R105m out of commissions/merchandise & admin — **no GP or trading-profit impact**. Implication: FY25 comparatives (turnover R119,049m, revenue R122,458m) are the correct base for LFL and margin forecasting; do not use previously reported figures. Verify LFL +1.04% and restated segment splits in D006/D007.

- **Segment footnote `[^#]`** `[p. 47]`: Confirms restatement allocation by segment and geography (PnP SA R176m, PnP RoA R10m, Boxer SA R250m, Boxer RoA R3m). Implication: regional turnover (SA R116,402m, RoA R3,888m) is restated — use for geographic growth modelling.

- **Segment footnote `*`** `[p. 46]`: "The Pick n Pay segment earned dividends from the Boxer segment of R136 million (2025: R9,260m), removed on consolidation." Implication: intra-group dividend flows are large and distort segment comparability; FY25 R9,260m is a one-off (Boxer IPO-related) — exclude from underlying segment earnings.

- **Segment footnote `**`** `[p. 46]`: Defines segmental trading profit = PBT before net finance costs and capital items. Implication: trading profit R1,685m is the EBITDA-proxy driver; capital items R442m (disposals R51m + impairments R391m) are below-the-line.

- **Segment footnote `***`** `[p. 46]`: Non-current assets = PPE + ROUA + intangibles + operating lease assets + non-current held for sale. Implication: R21,061m asset base for impairment/return modelling.

- **Note 11.1 footnote `*`** `[p. 56]`: Botswana franchise acquisition converted outstanding franchise receivable to intercompany debt, eliminated on consolidation — drove the R366m allowance release and the 14.4%→6.7% allowance ratio drop. Implication: the ECL ratio improvement is **partly structural (portfolio mix), not purely credit-quality improvement** — critical caveat for forecasting debtor costs. Verify underlying satisfactory-paid % in D008/Note 32.

- **Note 11.1 narrative** `[p. 56]`: Write-offs include R167m still under legal enforcement (2025: R15m) — a sharp rise; flag as credit-quality deterioration signal despite lower allowance ratio.

- **Note 9 narrative** `[p. 55]`: Boxer R200m repaid post-period-end → zero long-term debt; covenants met (net debt/EBITDA 0.2 vs <2.5; interest cover 6.2:1 vs >3.5:1); ZARONIA transition ongoing, no amendments yet. Implication: near-zero funding finance costs in FY27 forecast; watch ZARONIA repricing.

- **Note 13 footnotes** `[p. 57]`: Gift card forfeiture 10.7% (2025: 11.5%); loyalty forfeiture 19.0% (2025: 24.0%); refund liability R26m, right-of-return asset R22m. Implication: deferred revenue R377m (up from R300m) — higher loyalty redemption assumptions affect turnover recognition timing.

- **Note 10 narrative** `[p. 55]`: Inventory write-downs to NRV R425m (2025: R344m), +23.5%; provision R496m (2025: R421m). Implication: rising markdown/shrinkage pressure — feeds gross margin bridge; verify in D006/Note 10 detail.

- **Note 6.3 B-share narrative** `[p. 52]`: 105,186,384 B shares "unstapled" and to be repurchased for R0.00001 and cancelled subject to AGM approval. Implication: control/voting structure change post-Ackerman selldown — relevant to NCI and control-premium assumptions, not core forecast drivers.

- **Note 3.2 auditor footnote `*`** `[p. 44]`: Non-audit services R95,970 (2025: R25,000) — immaterial but note the jump.

### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

- **Q31 [Medium] — Confirm DPS = 0 (no parent dividend), NCI dividends R71m, share buyback R101m; check dividend policy.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D004/D003)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: The **Company** statement of changes in equity `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 86]` shows **no dividend paid by the parent** in either FY26 or FY25 — retained earnings moved only by profit for the period (FY25: R165m; FY26: Rnil). This is consistent with DPS = 0 at Company level. However, the **NCI dividends R71m** and **share buyback R101m** are **Group** cash-flow/equity items and are **not visible** in this Company-only capture; they remain open for D004/D003. Dividend policy statement also not in this section.

- **Q35 [Low] — Confirm share count 745,657k, treasury shares, and rights offer proceeds in equity.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D003/D004)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Rights offer proceeds **R3,877m** confirmed in Company statement of changes in equity `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 86]` (share capital +R3,877m, FY25). Share capital R3,883m and share premium R835m at 1 March 2026 `[p. 85, p. 86]`. **Share count 745,657k and treasury shares are not disclosed in this Company section** — remain open.

- **Q23 [Medium] — confirm DPS = 0, NCI dividends R71m, buyback R101m, dividend policy.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D004)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: As Q31 — parent DPS = 0 corroborated at Company level `[p. 86]`; NCI dividends, buyback and dividend policy not in this capture.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Note references 7.1, 7.2, 8.1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8.2 appear in the Company statements but their footnote/note definitions are NOT included in this section capture.** Specifically:
  - Note **7.1** (dividend income R20m FY26 vs Rnil FY25) `[p. 84]` — definition missing; must confirm it is dividend from subsidiary and reconcile to Group dividend income R25m (Q6).
  - Note **7.2** (receivables from related entities R65m; R26m repaid) `[p. 85, p. 87]` — definition missing.
  - Note **8.1** (ECL recovery Rnil FY26 vs R187m FY25) `[p. 84]` — definition missing; the FY25 R187m recovery is a large one-off that flatters FY25 Company profit and must be understood (reversal of prior impairment of subsidiary loan?).
  - Note **2** (administration expenses R20m vs R28m) `[p. 84]` — definition missing.
  - Note **3** (tax Rnil both years) `[p. 84]` — definition missing; confirm no tax charge despite FY25 profit R165m (likely dividend/participation exemption or assessed loss).
  - Note **4** (investment in subsidiary R4,700m) `[p. 85]` — definition missing; confirm this is PnP/Boxer holding and whether Boxer deconsolidation (Q11/Q30) affects it.
  - Note **5** (cash R7m) `[p. 85]` — definition missing.
  - Note **6** (share capital R3,883m) `[p. 85]` — definition missing; ties to share count Q35.
  - Note **8.2** (trade and other payables R1m vs R7m) `[p. 85]` — definition missing.
- **Key qualification implication**: The Company P&L is essentially a **holding-company pass-through** (dividend income R20m less admin R20m = nil; FY25 boosted by R187m ECL recovery and R6m finance income). It carries **no forecasting signal for Group trading** but does confirm: (i) **no parent dividend declared** (DPS = 0), and (ii) **rights offer R3,877m** fully booked to equity in FY25. The **FY25 R187m ECL recovery** is a one-off that must be excluded from any normalised Company earnings and checked against Group Note 11 (Q7/Q18/Q26) to ensure it is not double-counted at Group level.

      6   Share capital continued                                                 
      6.1 Ordinary share capital continued                                        
                                                                                  
          During the prior period, the Company undertook the following:           
          ▪ As resolved by shareholders at the general meeting held on 26 June 2024, the Company amended its Memorandum of
           Incorporation to increase its authorised ordinary share capital to 10 billion shares and converted all ordinary shares to no
           par value. Subsequent to this, as resolved at the general meeting held on 1 October 2024, the Company reduced its authorised
           ordinary share capital to 828 500 000 shares, ensuring that the number of unissued ordinary shares constituted no more than
           10% of the total number of authorised ordinary shares post the rights offer.
          ▪ The Company concluded a fully underwritten renounceable rights offer share issue (“rights offer”) during August 2024, which
           raised gross proceeds of R4.0 billion. The rights offer consisted of an offer of 252 206 809 new ordinary shares. Qualifying
           Shareholders who held no par value ordinary shares in the issued share capital of PIK (“PIK Shares”) on the Record Date
           received 51.11 rights for every 100 existing PIK Shares held. Each right entitled the holder to subscribe for one new PIK Share
           at a subscription price of 1 586.0 cents (ZAR15.86) (“Rights Offer Share Price”) per Rights Offer Share. The rights offer raised
           R3.9 billion of new equity capital, net of transaction costs of R0.1 billion. All necessary resolutions to effect the rights offer were
           passed by the requisite majority of shareholders at the Company’s general meeting held on 26 June 2024.
          Refer to note 7.3 and 7.4 for details of directors’ interest in shares. 
          The Company did not declare dividends during the current or prior period.

      6.2 B share capital                                                         
          Authorised unlisted, non-convertible, non-participating, no par value B shares 361 500 361 500
          Issued unlisted, non-convertible, non-participating, no par value B shares 325 426 325 426
          The holders of B shares are not entitled to any rights to distributions by the Company or any other economic benefits.
          B shares are stapled to certain ordinary shares, constituting a B-share ratio for every one stapled ordinary share. B shares cannot
          be traded separately from stapled ordinary shares, and together are subject to restrictions upon disposal.
          During the prior period, the Company undertook the following:           
          ▪ As resolved by shareholders at the general meeting held on 26 June 2024, the Company amended its Memorandum of
           Incorporation to increase its authorised B share capital to 5.3 billion shares. Subsequent to this, at the general meeting held on
           1 October 2024, the Company reduced authorised B share capital to 361 500 000 shares, ensuring that the number of unissued
           B shares constituted no more than 10% of the total number of authorised B shares.
          ▪ The Company concluded a rights offer during August 2024 (refer to note 6.1 for further information). According to the terms
           of the B shares, an “Adjustment Event” such as a rights offer, triggers the issuance of additional B shares to B shareholders,
           maintaining the B Share Issue Ratio. However, following a resolution passed at the general meeting on 26 June 2024, and in line
           with the controlling shareholder’s commitment to ordinary shareholders, B shareholders agreed to reduce the B Share Issue Ratio
           from 1.98061 to 1.64254 B shares for every one stapled ordinary share. This adjustment lowered the controlling shareholder’s
           aggregate voting rights from 52% to 49%. As a result, 65 743 295 new B Shares were issued to stapled ordinary shareholders.
          As previously announced, Ackerman Investment Holdings (RF) Proprietary Limited and its related and inter-related persons
          (collectively, the “Ackerman Family”) disposed of 64 038 857 ordinary shares on 17 November 2025 and the 105 186 384 B shares
          held by the Ackerman Family that were previously attached to such ordinary shares have ceased to have voting rights. Subject
          to the requisite shareholder approval being obtained at the 2026 AGM, these “unstapled” B shares will be repurchased by the
          Company for a nominal price of R0.00001 per B share and cancelled, as contemplated in the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI).
          Refer to note 7.3 and 7.4 for details of directors’ interest in shares.

      8   Financial instruments                                                   
          Overview                                                                
                                                                                  
          The Company is exposed to risk in respect of financial instruments, namely the receivables from related entities, cash and cash
          equivalents, and trade and other payables. Market risk is negated as financial assets and liabilities have no exposure to changes
          in exchange rates, or equity prices and have limited exposure to changes in interest rates.
      8.1 Credit risk                                                             
          Credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Company if a counterparty to a financial instrument fails to meet its contractual
          obligations. Financial assets, which potentially subject the Company to credit risk, consist of the receivables from related entities,
          and cash.                                                               
          Credit risk of receivables from related entities                        
          The Company applies a general approach for measuring impairment losses on the receivables from related entities, at an amount
          equal to expected credit losses, taking into account past experience and future macro-economic factors, including estimated
          profits and cash forecasts. Management has assessed that the receivables from Pick n Pay Retailers Limited and Pick n Pay
          Employee Share Purchase Trust are fully recoverable. The credit risk is considered to be low, and no impairment losses have
          been recognised.                                                        
          Credit risk of financial guarantee contracts                            
          In the prior period the Company reversed the expected credit loss allowance of R187 million as the guarantee in favour of the
          debt facilities of its subsidiary, Pick n Pay Retailers Proprietary Limited, was terminated on repayment of those debt facilities,
          removing the exposure to counterparty (Pick n Pay Retailers Proprietary Limited) credit risk.
          Cash and cash equivalents                                               
          The Company’s cash is placed with a major South African institution, which at period end had a high credit standing and had a
          long-term credit rating of zaAAA (2025: zaAA).                          
      8.2 Liquidity risk                                                          
          Liquidity risk is the risk that the Company will not be able to meet its financial obligations as they fall due.
          The following are the contractual undiscounted cashflows of financial liabilities, including estimated interest payments:

      9   Going concern                                                           
          The Board of directors (the Board) has performed a formal review of the Company and its subsidiaries’ ability to continue trading
          as a going concern in the foreseeable future. As part of this review, the Board has considered the impact of the current economic
          environment, reviewed current trading trends, interrogated the Company’s forward-looking financial forecasts, considered the
          adequacy of insurance covers and assessed the Company’s solvency and liquidity following the recapitalisation in the prior year.
          The Board is satisfied as to the Company’s ability to continue as going concern for the foreseeable future and has concluded that
          the presentation of the Company annual financial statements on a going concern basis is appropriate.

      Appendix          2                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Independent Auditor’s Assurance Report on the Compilation of Pro Forma      
      Financial Information included in the Group Annual Financial Statements for the
      52 weeks ended 1 March 2026                                                 
                                                                                  
      The Directors of Pick n Pay Stores Limited                                  
      We have completed our assurance engagement to report on the compilation of pro forma financial information of Pick n Pay Stores and
      its subsidiaries (collectively the “Group”), by the directors.              
      The pro forma financial information, as set out on pages 93 to 94 of the Group Annual Financial Statements for the 52 weeks ended
      1 March 2026, consists of the i) Net cash/debt (excluding lease liabilities) and Net cash/debt (including lease liabilities), ii) EBITDA and
      EBITDA (pre-IFRS 16), iii) Trading profit after lease interest for the 52 weeks ending 1 March 2026 and related notes, (collectively, the
      “Pro Forma Financial Information”). The applicable criteria on the basis of which the directors have compiled the Pro Forma Financial
      Information are specified in the JSE Limited (“JSE”) Listings Requirements and described in page 93 of the Group Annual Financial
      Statements for the 52 weeks ended 1 March 2026.                             
      The Pro Forma Financial Information has been compiled by the directors to illustrate the additional financial measures regularly used by
      the management of the Group to assess operating performance and financial position and thereby enhance an investor’s understanding
      of the Group’s results of operations and financial performance. As part of this process, information about the Group’s financial position
      and financial performance has been extracted by the directors from the Group’s annual financial statements for the 52 weeks ended
      1 March 2026, on which an auditor’s report was issued on 22 May 2026.       
      Directors’ Responsibility for the Pro Forma Financial Information           
      The directors are responsible for compiling the Pro Forma Financial Information on the basis of the applicable criteria specified in the
      JSE Listings Requirements, described on page 93 of the Group Annual Financial Statements for the 52 weeks ended 1 March 2026.
      Our Independence and Quality Management                                     
      We have complied with the independence and other ethical requirements of the Code of Professional Conduct for Registered Auditors
      issued by the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA Code), which is founded on fundamental principles of integrity,
      objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour. The IRBA Code is consistent with the
      corresponding sections of the International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants’ International Code of Ethics for Professional
      Accountants (including International Independence Standards).               
      The firm applies International Standard on Quality Management 1 (ISQM 1) Quality Management for Firms that Perform Audits or
      Reviews of Financial Statements, or Other Assurance or Related Services Engagements which requires the firm to design, implement and
      operate a system of quality management, including documented policies or procedures regarding compliance with ethical requirements,
      professional standards and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

      Auditor’s Responsibility                                                    
      Our responsibility is to express an opinion about whether the Pro Forma Financial Information has been compiled, in all material
      respects, by the directors on the basis specified in the JSE Listings Requirements and described on page 93 of the Group Annual Financial
      Statements for the 52 weeks ended 1 March 2026, based on our procedures performed.
      We conducted our engagement in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements (ISAE) 3420, Assurance
      Engagements to Report on the Compilation of Pro forma Financial Information Included in a Prospectus, which is applicable to an
      engagement of this nature, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. This standard requires that we comply
      with ethical requirements and plan and perform our procedures to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the Pro Forma Financial
      Information has been compiled, in all material respects, on the basis specified in the JSE Listings Requirements.
      For purposes of this engagement, we are not responsible for updating or reissuing any reports or opinions on any historical financial
      information used in compiling the Pro Forma Financial Information, nor have we, in the course of this engagement, performed an audit
      or review of the financial information used in compiling the Pro Forma Financial Information.
      The purpose of the Pro Forma Financial Information included in the Group Annual Financial Statements for the 52 weeks ended
      1 March 2026, is to illustrate how the unadjusted financial information of the entity has been impacted by the adjustments made, as
      described in the basis of preparation. Accordingly, we do not provide any assurance that the actual outcome of the adjustments made
      would have been as presented.                                               
      A reasonable assurance engagement to report on whether the Pro Forma Financial Information has been compiled, in all material
      respects, on the basis of the applicable criteria involves performing procedures to assess whether the applicable criteria used by the
      directors in the compilation of the Pro Forma Financial Information provides a reasonable basis for presenting the significant effects
      directly attributable to the adjustments made, and to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about whether:
      ▪ The related pro forma adjustments give appropriate effect to those criteria; and
      ▪ The Pro Forma Financial Information reflects the proper application of those adjustments to the unadjusted financial information.
      Our procedures selected depend on our judgment, having regard to our understanding of the nature of the Group and the adjustments
      made in respect of which the Pro Forma Financial Information has been compiled, and other relevant engagement circumstances.
      Our engagement also involves evaluating the overall presentation of the Pro Forma Financial Information.
      We believe that the evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.
      Opinion                                                                     
      In our opinion, the Pro Forma Financial Information has been compiled, in all material respects, on the basis specified in the JSE Listings
      Requirements, described on page 93 of the Group Annual Financial Statements for the 52 weeks ended 1 March 2026.

      Appendix          3                                                         
                                                                                  
                                                                                  
      Like-for-like turnover and forward looking information                      
      Additional information may not represent a defined term under IFRS Accounting Standards and, as a result, it may not be comparable
      with similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Additional information is the responsibility of the Board of directors of the
      Group, is presented for illustrative purposes only and has not been reviewed nor reported on by the Group’s external auditors.
      1   Like-for-like turnover and expense growth comparisons                   
          Like-for-like (“LfL”) turnover growth comparisons relate to stores that have been open for at least 12 months, removing the impact
          of store openings, closures and conversions in the current and previous reporting periods, and in the current period removes the
          impact of the amended franchise model. This franchise model offers a higher purchasing rebate to our franchisees (recorded
          against turnover) in exchange for a higher franchise royalty fee (recorded in other income). LfL turnover on new or closed
          adjacent liquor stores inherits the LfL indicator of the store that it is attached to, as this is the manner in which the Group
          manages its store base. This is not the case for new or closed stand-alone liquor and clothing stores.
          LfL expense growth comparisons remove the impact of store openings, closures and conversions, and the movement in the ECL
          allowance, in the current and previous reporting periods.               
      2   Forward looking information                                             
          These annual financial statements contain certain forward-looking statements related to the Group’s possible future actions,
          long-term strategy, performance, liquidity position and financial position which, although based on assumptions and/or estimates
          that the Group considers reasonable, are subject to risks and uncertainties which could cause actual events or conditions to differ
          materially from those expressed or implied by the forward looking statements. All forward looking statements are solely based
          on the views and considerations of the Board, and in particular, as at the date hereof. The Group does not undertake to update or
          revise any of these forward looking statements publicly, whether to reflect new information, future events or otherwise. These
          forward looking statements have not been reviewed or reported on by the Group’s external auditors.

### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

- **Q35 [Low] — Confirm share count 745,657k, treasury shares, tie to Group equity.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D003/D005)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Issued ordinary shares confirmed at **745,657 thousand** (745,657,130 per shareholder analysis) `[unmapped, physical PDF p. 90; p. 100]`. Issued share capital **R3,883m** confirmed `[p. 90]`. B shares issued **325,426 thousand** `[p. 91; p. 101]`. **Remainder open**: treasury shares are not disclosed as a separate line in this capture — the shareholder analysis shows total shares 745,657,130 with no treasury deduction visible; the RSP-held shares (4,554,727) and Employee Share Purchase Trust (1,716,680) are shown as non-public holders, not explicitly as treasury. Tie of R3,883m share capital + premium to Group equity still requires the Group statement of changes in equity (D003).

- **Q41 [Low] — Tie Company share capital R3,883m + premium R835m to Group share count 745,657k and treasury shares.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D003)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Share capital **R3,883m** confirmed `[p. 90]`; share count **745,657k** confirmed `[p. 90; p. 100]`. Share premium R835m is **not shown in this capture** (only "Issued share capital R3,883m" appears). Remainder open for Group equity reconciliation.

- **Q40 [Low] — Whether Boxer deconsolidation/sale triggers impairment/reclassification of Company investment in subsidiary R4,700m.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Investment in subsidiary **Pick n Pay Retailers Proprietary Limited — shares at cost R4,700m** (2025: R4,700m), no impairment recognised `[p. 90]`. Note 4 confirms PnP Retailers is a wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated in RSA. No mention of Boxer deconsolidation impact on this carrying value in this capture. Remainder open — subsequent-events note (D012) must confirm whether the Boxer transaction sits below PnP Retailers and whether any impairment indicator arises.

- **Q39 [Medium] — Basis of Company nil tax on FY25 profit R165m and that it does not affect Group ETR.**
  - **Status**: `Resolved`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Company current and deferred tax **nil** in both periods; no tax paid `[p. 90]`. Reconciliation: statutory tax nil (2025: R45m), exempt dividend income R(5)m, unrecognised tax losses R4m, non-deductible admin R1m, non-deductible ECL allowance nil (2025: R(51)m) → effective tax **nil** `[p. 90]`. Cumulative unused tax loss **R34.9m** (2025: R17.8m), available indefinitely `[p. 90]`. This is a standalone Company reconciliation and does not feed Group ETR.

- **Q42 [Medium] — Obtain definitions of Company notes 2–8 (footnote text missing).**
  - **Status**: `Resolved`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Note 2 = Administration expenses (2.1 Directors' remuneration; 2.2 Auditor's remuneration R276,700 / 2025 R264,800) `[p. 89]`; Note 3 = Tax `[p. 90]`; Note 4 = Investment in subsidiary `[p. 90]`; Note 5 = Cash and cash equivalents (R7m / 2025 R6m) `[p. 90]`; Note 6 = Share capital (6.1 ordinary, 6.2 B shares) `[p. 90–91]`; Note 7 = Related party transactions (7.1 dividend income, 7.2 receivables, 7.3/7.4 directors' interests, 7.5 KMP) `[p. 92]`; Note 8 = Financial instruments (8.1 credit risk, 8.2 liquidity risk, 8.3 capital management) `[p. 93]`.

- **Q37 [High] — Confirm Company ECL recovery R187m FY25 is a subsidiary-loan reversal and NOT in Group Note 11 ECL charge R230m.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D008)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Confirmed the R187m reversal relates to the **financial guarantee contract** in favour of PnP Retailers' debt facilities, terminated on repayment of those facilities, removing counterparty credit risk `[p. 93]`. This is a Company-level guarantee ECL reversal, distinct in nature from Group Note 11 trade-receivable ECL. Remainder open: confirm it is not double-counted in Group Note 11 R230m charge (D008).

- **Q38 [Medium] — Reconcile Company dividend income R20m (Note 7.1) to Group Note 2 dividend line R25m; explain R5m difference.**
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D006)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Company Note 7.1 dividend income = **R20m** (PnP Employee Share Purchase Trust R14m + PnP Retailers R6m; 2025: nil) `[p. 92]`. Group Note 2 dividend line R25m not in this capture. R5m difference remains open for D006.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Note 2.1 directors' remuneration footnotes `[p. 89]`**: `[^1]` Gareth Ackerman retired as Chairman 5 Aug 2025; James Formby appointed Chairman same date. `[^2]` Pooven Viranna appointed 1 June 2025; David Friedland retired 5 Aug 2025. `[^3]` Thabo Leeuw and Grant Pattison appointed 1 Feb 2026. `[^4]` Mariam Cassim resigned 5 July 2024. `[^5]` David Robins retired 27 Aug 2024. `*` Formby's fee includes lead independent director fee pre-chairmanship. **Implication**: board churn explains the FY26 total remuneration drop to R11,824k (2025: R14,282k); no forecast driver beyond governance, but confirms Chairman transition timing relevant to any strategic-disposal (Boxer) governance narrative.

- **Note 3 tax footnote `*` `[p. 90]`**: "The reconciliation of effective tax has been presented in South African rand values and the comparative period has been amended for comparability purposes." **Implication**: prior-period tax recon was restated for presentation only; no P&L effect. Confirms Company tax is a standalone holding-company reconciliation (statutory tax nil vs R45m prior), driven by exempt dividends and unrecognised losses — not a Group ETR input.

- **Note 6.1 rights offer narrative `[p. 91]`**: Rights offer raised **gross R4.0bn**, **net R3.9bn** after R0.1bn transaction costs; 252,206,809 new shares at ZAR15.86; 51.11 rights per 100 shares. **Implication**: reconciles to the R3,877m rights-offer equity figure carried in Q35/Q36 — net proceeds R3.9bn ≈ R3,877m. Confirms no dividend declared current or prior period (supports Q23/Q31/Q36 DPS = 0).

- **Note 6.2 B-share narrative `[p. 91]`**: B Share Issue Ratio reduced from 1.98061 to 1.64254, lowering controlling shareholder voting from **52% to 49%**; 65,743,295 new B shares issued. Ackerman Family disposed of **64,038,857 ordinary shares** on 17 Nov 2025 and **105,186,384 B shares** ceased to have voting rights; subject to 2026 AGM approval these will be repurchased at R0.00001 and cancelled. **Implication**: material control/governance change — Ackerman Family now below 50%; relevant to any related-party or disposal decisions (Boxer). B-share repurchase is nominal (immaterial cash), but dilution/voting shift matters for shareholder-resolution risk on the Boxer sale (s.189A-type approvals).

- **Note 7.2 receivables qualification `[p. 92]`**: Receivables from related entities **R65m** (PnP Retailers R51m + ESP Trust R14m), "unsecured, interest-free, repayable on demand," carrying value approximates fair value. **Implication**: no ECL recognised (Note 8.1) — Company asserts full recoverability; low forecast relevance but confirms no hidden credit loss at holdco.

- **Note 8.1 credit-risk qualification `[p. 93]`**: "Management has assessed that the receivables from PnP Retailers and ESP Trust are **fully recoverable**… no impairment losses recognised." Cash placed with major SA institution rated **zaAAA (2025: zaAA)**. **Implication**: rating upgrade noted; no Company-level ECL charge FY26 (vs R187m reversal FY25). Confirms the R187m is a guarantee reversal, not trade ECL.

- **Note 8.2 liquidity `[p. 93]`**: Trade and other payables contractual cash flows **R1m** (2025: R7m), all repayable within 1 year. **Implication**: holdco is essentially debt-free at Company level; consistent with Group net cash R3,077m (Q14).

- **Note 9 going concern `[p. 93]`**: Board satisfied; references "recapitalisation in the prior year" (rights offer) and "current economic environment / trading trends." **Implication**: no going-concern EOM; supports unqualified opinion (Q1).

- **Appendix 1 week-53 footnote `[^#]` `[p. 95]`**: Restatement increased prior-period turnover for 53 weeks by **R439m** (Group), PnP SA R186m, PnP RoA R176m, Boxer R10m, and **R253m** respectively (note: the footnote lists five figures against four named segments — a presentation inconsistency); for 52 weeks by **R429m** Group, PnP SA R182m, PnP RoA R172m, Boxer R10m, **R247m** — again five values for four labels. "No net impact on gross profit, trading profit, or loss." **Implication**: confirms Q17 restatement (+R439m 53-week / +R429m 52-week). **Flag**: the footnote's segment attribution appears internally inconsistent (five amounts, four segments) — verify segment-level restatement split in D006/D007.

- **Appendix 1 net cash/debt footnote `[^#]` `[p. 95]`**: Intragroup receivable/(payable) of **R(371)m PnP / R371m Boxer** "represent operational cash flow balances between the entities and were repaid shortly after year end." **Implication**: nets to zero at Group; confirms no genuine Group debt. Group net cash excl. leases **R3,077m**; net debt incl. leases **R(15,458)m** (2025: R(14,942)m) — lease liabilities **R18,535m** (non-current R15,883m + current R2,652m) `[p. 95]`, consistent with Q14.

- **Appendix 1 EBITDA/TPAL footnotes `*`/`**` `[p. 96]`**: `*` PnP and Boxer columns "extracted, without adjustment, from the Group's accounting records" (unaudited); `**` Group column from audited AFS with unqualified assurance. **Implication**: **segment-level EBITDA/TPAL figures are unaudited management records** — treat PnP vs Boxer splits with caution in the forecast; only Group totals are audited. This is a key qualification for segment margin modelling.

- **Appendix 3 LfL footnote `[p. 99]`**: LfL "removes the impact of the amended franchise model" — higher purchasing rebate to franchisees (recorded **against turnover**) in exchange for higher franchise royalty (recorded in **other income**). LfL expense growth removes ECL allowance movement. Forward-looking statements "not reviewed or reported on by external auditors." **Implication**: the franchise-model change **depresses reported turnover and shifts margin to other income** — critical for revenue decomposition and gross-margin bridge; explains PnP turnover decline (73,608 vs 74,798) partly structural, not purely volume. Must separate franchise rebate effect from underlying LfL.

- **Appendix 2 auditor's report `[p. 97–98]`**: Pro forma (net cash/debt, EBITDA, EBITDA pre-IFRS 16, TPAL) covered by unqualified ISAE 3420 assurance; audit report dated **22 May 2026**. **Implication**: pro forma metrics (EBITDA R5,640m; EBITDA pre-IFRS 16 R1,613m; TPAL R122m) are assured as to compilation, not as to outcome.
